बॉक्स ऑफिस पर आ गया है महा-तूफान, रणबीर कपूर और यश का धमाकेदार जलवा बरकरार! 🔥

फिल्म Ramayana Part One ने अपने तीसरे Saturday को बॉक्स ऑफिस पर जबरदस्त बढ़त हासिल कर ली है। 🎬

Ranbir Kapoor और Yash स्टारर यह फिल्म सिनेमाघरों में लगातार तूफानी कमाई कर रही है। 📈

रिपोर्ट्स के अनुसार, 3rd Saturday की इस बेहतरीन ग्रोथ के साथ फिल्म आज 900 Cr का आंकड़ा पार करने के लिए पूरी तरह तैयार है। 💥

इसे अब तक की Biggest Indian film माना जा रहा है, जिसके इकोनॉमिक्स और कलेक्शन के नंबर्स ने सबको हैरान कर दिया है।

क्या आपने फिल्म Ramayana Part One सिनेमाघरों में देख ली है? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Decoding Economics of Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer Ramayana Part One: The numbers behind Biggest Indian film ever
ctx.summary:
Ramayana: Part One is entering the final stages of its first theatrical run. As of yesterday, the film has grossed Rs. 1592 crore approx globally. It is expected to close its run at around Rs. 1825 crore. With the theatrical business now largely known, it is time to look at the highly anticipated economics of the film.  
 Before diving in, an important note. Unlike most films, whose revenue picture is largely complete once their theatrical run ends, Ramayana: Part One still has significant recoveries to come. These include the second-phase overseas release, along with the sale of digital and television rights for the international versions. As a result, the economics presented below are not the final picture. While one could wait until the second-phase overseas release, there is still no official timeline for it. It could be three months, six months, or even later. No say. 
 Ramayana is the costliest film made in the history of Indian cinema. Since it's a two-parter, the costs are shared in two films. While it is entirely possible that one instalment cost more than the other, there is no reliable split available, so for the purpose of this analysis, the costs have simply been divided equally. The cost of production for this film is said to be Rs. 1200 crore. This excludes a tax rebate from the UK and Canada, which is expected to be around Rs. 300 crore. Accounting for that gives a net COP of Rs. 900 crore for the film.
